trace.situation: One of the two auxiliary scavenge air blowers fails to start when the engine is ordered to start, leaving only one blower to provide scavenging air during the low-load starting phase. The remaining blower can maintain operation but with reduced margin, and if it also fails, the engine cannot be started safely.
trace.trigger: Auxiliary blower 'failed to start' alarm with only one blower running indication on ECR panel

procedures.action: Check the local starter panel and motor protection relay for the tripped blower for an overload or phase failure indication.
procedures.why: Most single-blower start failures are caused by thermal overload trip or a blown fuse in the starter panel, which must be identified before reset.

procedures.action: Reset the overload/trip locally if safe and attempt a manual start of the blower from the ECR panel in manual mode.
procedures.why: Confirms whether the fault was a transient trip or a genuine motor/mechanical fault requiring further isolation.

procedures.action: If the blower will not restart, keep the engine running on the single operating blower and inform the bridge of reduced scavenging redundancy, limiting load increases until repaired.
procedures.why: The system is designed to run on one blower in emergency mode, but loss of the second blower removes all redundancy for low-load and starting conditions.

constraints: Auxiliary blowers must be running below approx. 25-35% engine load before the non-return valves open to turbocharger-only scavenging
Engine start is automatically delayed until blowers are confirmed running
regulations: Manufacturer requirement: minimum two auxiliary blowers must be available per engine configuration
warnings: If both auxiliary blowers are unavailable, the engine cannot achieve adequate scavenging at low load and must not be started or maneuvered
outcomes: Loss of both blowers risks incomplete scavenging, poor combustion, and failed starts or stalling at low load
Prompt repair restores full redundancy and safe maneuvering capability
key_facts: Auxiliary blowers start automatically below approx. 25-35% load and stop above approx. 30-40% load with hysteresis
A minimum of two electrically driven auxiliary blowers is fitted per engine
Blowers are integrated in the reversing chamber below the scavenge air cooler

question_seeds.text: What should I check first if one auxiliary blower fails to start before engine start?
Why does the engine start sequence delay automatically when a blower hasn't started yet?

known_issue.failure_mode: auxiliary blower start failure (single unit)
known_issue.detection_method: ECR blower status alarm / motor starter panel trip indication

trace.situation: Both auxiliary scavenge air blowers are unavailable simultaneously, due to a common power supply fault or sequential mechanical failures, removing all forced scavenging air supply below the auxiliary blower cut-in load. This is a critical condition that prevents safe engine starting and can cause severe under-scavenging if it occurs while running at low load.
trace.trigger: Simultaneous 'auxiliary blower stopped' alarms for both units combined with falling scavenge air receiver pressure at low load

procedures.action: Verify the common power supply (switchboard breaker, feeder) to both auxiliary blower starter panels.
procedures.why: A shared electrical fault such as a tripped bus-tie or feeder breaker is a common cause of simultaneous loss of both blowers.

procedures.action: If power is confirmed healthy, inspect each starter panel individually for independent faults and attempt manual restart.
procedures.why: Distinguishes between a shared electrical cause and coincidental independent mechanical failures.

procedures.action: If blowers cannot be restored, do not attempt to start or increase load on the engine; hold at current load or stop safely per bridge coordination.
procedures.why: Without any auxiliary blower, insufficient scavenge air at low load leads to incomplete combustion, overheating, and potential turbocharger surge.

constraints: Engine start is interlocked to require confirmed blower operation before fuel admission
Scavenge air pressure must remain above the designed minimum for stable combustion at low load
regulations: Classification society requirement for redundant scavenging air supply at low load conditions
warnings: Attempting to start or run the engine without any auxiliary blower operative can cause severe under-scavenging, high exhaust temperatures, and scavenge fire risk
outcomes: Continued operation without blowers risks engine shutdown, turbocharger surge, or scavenge fire
Restoring at least one blower allows safe continued operation per emergency running provision
key_facts: If one auxiliary blower is out of service, the system is designed to run on the remaining blower without manual valve adjustment
Loss of both blowers removes all forced scavenging below turbocharger self-sustaining load

question_seeds.text: When should the engine be prevented from starting due to loss of both auxiliary blowers?
How do I distinguish a shared electrical fault from independent blower failures?

known_issue.failure_mode: complete loss of auxiliary blower scavenging
known_issue.detection_method: dual blower alarm combined with scavenge air pressure drop

trace.situation: A non-return valve between the scavenge air cooler and the scavenge air receiver fails to close fully after the auxiliary blowers stop, allowing hot compressed air from the turbocharger side to leak back through the blower discharge path. This reduces blower efficiency and can cause blower overheating or reduced receiver pressure at low load.
trace.trigger: Elevated auxiliary blower motor current and reduced scavenge air receiver pressure despite blowers confirmed running

procedures.action: Confirm blower running status and motor current against the normal baseline for the vessel.
procedures.why: Elevated current with low delivered pressure indicates the blower is working against backflow rather than pure receiver demand.

procedures.action: During the next engine stop, inspect the non-return valve flap and seat in the reversing chamber for wear, sticking, or debris.
procedures.why: A worn or fouled flap will not seal fully, allowing recirculation that masks as reduced blower performance.

procedures.action: Replace or recondition the valve flap/seat and verify free movement before returning to service.
procedures.why: Restoring proper sealing ensures the blower is not working against backflow and protects it from thermal overload.

constraints: Non-return valves must close fully when auxiliary blowers are running to prevent backflow from the turbocharger side
regulations: Manufacturer maintenance requirement for periodic inspection of scavenge air non-return valves
warnings: Continued operation with a leaking non-return valve can overheat the auxiliary blower motor and eventually trip it on overload, reducing blower redundancy
outcomes: Uncorrected backflow leads to chronic blower overload trips and premature motor failure
Valve repair restores correct blower loading and receiver pressure control
key_facts: Non-return valves are fitted between the scavenge air cooler and receiver and close automatically when auxiliary blowers start supplying air
They are mechanically actuated by differential pressure, not electrically controlled

question_seeds.text: Which component should be inspected if blower current is high but receiver pressure stays low?
Why does a leaking non-return valve cause blower overheating?

known_issue.failure_mode: non-return valve leakage / backflow
known_issue.detection_method: blower motor current trend analysis vs receiver pressure

trace.situation: The non-return valve on the auxiliary blower discharge sticks in the closed position after the blower has started delivering air, blocking the flow path into the scavenge air receiver even though the blower is running. This can starve the receiver of air during low-load operation despite the blower appearing to function normally.
trace.trigger: Scavenge air receiver pressure fails to rise despite confirmed auxiliary blower running and normal motor current

procedures.action: Verify blower discharge pressure locally at the reversing chamber versus receiver inlet pressure.
procedures.why: A large differential confirms the flow path is blocked downstream of the blower rather than a blower output problem.

procedures.action: Stop the engine safely and physically inspect the non-return valve for a seized or jammed flap.
procedures.why: Mechanical seizure, often from corrosion or carbon buildup, is the typical cause of a valve stuck closed.

procedures.action: Free, clean, or replace the valve mechanism and verify smooth opening before resuming operation.
procedures.why: Restores proper airflow path so the auxiliary blower can effectively supply the receiver during low-load running.

constraints: Receiver pressure must track blower delivery when auxiliary blowers are in operation
regulations: Manufacturer requirement for unobstructed non-return valve operation to maintain scavenging during low-load running
warnings: If undetected, this fault can mimic a blower failure and lead to incorrect troubleshooting, delaying restoration of adequate scavenge air
outcomes: Continued blockage results in poor low-load combustion and potential engine trip on low scavenge pressure
Freeing the valve restores correct air delivery and engine starting reliability
key_facts: Non-return valves open automatically under blower discharge pressure and require no manual adjustment under normal conditions
A seized valve can present as a blower fault at the control system level

question_seeds.text: How can I tell if a stuck non-return valve is the cause of low receiver pressure rather than the blower itself?

known_issue.failure_mode: non-return valve seized closed
known_issue.detection_method: differential pressure check between blower discharge and receiver

trace.situation: Progressive fouling of the air-side fins of the scavenge air cooler reduces heat transfer efficiency, causing scavenge air temperature after the cooler to rise gradually over weeks of operation. This increases charge air temperature into the cylinders, raising exhaust temperatures and reducing engine efficiency.
trace.trigger: Gradual upward trend in scavenge air temperature after cooler, with exhaust gas temperatures rising at constant load

procedures.action: Trend scavenge air temperature after cooler against historical baseline at the same load and ambient condition.
procedures.why: Confirms a genuine fouling trend rather than a seasonal ambient temperature effect.

procedures.action: Schedule and perform air-side chemical cleaning of the cooler using the grease-dissolving media injected through the dedicated spray pipe connection, with the engine stopped.
procedures.why: Removes oil and soot deposits from the cooler fins that are restricting airflow and heat transfer; cleaning must be done at standstill per manufacturer instruction.

procedures.action: After cleaning, verify scavenge air temperature returns to baseline and inspect the drain box level switch and filter for cleaning residue.
procedures.why: Confirms effective cleaning and prevents cleaning agent residue from blocking the drain system.

constraints: Air cooler cleaning must be performed with engine at standstill
Drain water oil content must be checked below 15 ppm before overboard discharge
regulations: MARPOL Annex I oil content discharge limit of 15 ppm for drain water routed overboard
warnings: Prolonged fouling increases thermal loading on pistons and liners and can accelerate turbocharger fouling and surge risk
outcomes: Uncleaned coolers progressively raise exhaust temperatures, reduce efficiency, and increase fuel consumption
Scheduled cleaning restores design cooling performance and lowers exhaust temperature margins
key_facts: Air-side cleaning is done by injecting grease-dissolving media through the spray pipe above the cooler element
Sludge from cleaning drains to the drain water collecting tank and must pass an oil content check before overboard discharge

question_seeds.text: When should air cooler cleaning be scheduled based on scavenge air temperature trend?
What is the oil content limit for air cooler cleaning drain water before overboard discharge?

known_issue.failure_mode: scavenge air cooler air-side fouling
known_issue.detection_method: scavenge air temperature after cooler trend monitoring

trace.situation: Scale and biological fouling accumulate on the water (cooling medium) side of the scavenge air cooler, reducing heat exchange effectiveness independently of the air side. This manifests as high scavenge air temperature combined with a reduced cooling water temperature rise across the cooler.
trace.trigger: High scavenge air temperature after cooler with cooling water inlet/outlet temperature differential lower than normal

procedures.action: Check cooling water flow rate and inlet temperature to rule out a cooling water supply issue before suspecting the cooler itself.
procedures.why: Ensures the root cause is fouling inside the cooler and not reduced cooling water flow or an upstream heat exchanger problem.

procedures.action: Plan a water-side chemical descaling or mechanical cleaning of the cooler during the next scheduled engine stoppage.
procedures.why: Removes scale or biofouling from the water side tubes that air-side cleaning alone will not address.

procedures.action: After cleaning, verify both scavenge air temperature and cooling water differential return to design values.
procedures.why: Confirms the fouling has been removed and heat transfer capacity is restored.

constraints: Cooling water quality must be maintained per treatment program to minimize scale formation
regulations: Manufacturer cooling water treatment guidelines for central cooling systems
warnings: If both air-side and water-side fouling occur together, cooler performance can degrade rapidly and significantly shorten turbocharger life due to sustained high intake temperatures
outcomes: Untreated water-side fouling leads to persistent high scavenge air temperature despite air-side cleaning
Combined cleaning restores full design cooling capacity
key_facts: Scavenge air cooler cooling water data is specified per the vessel's chosen cooling water system design
Air-side cleaning does not address water-side scale or biological fouling

question_seeds.text: Why would scavenge air temperature stay high even after an air-side cooler cleaning?

known_issue.failure_mode: scavenge air cooler water-side fouling
known_issue.detection_method: cooling water temperature differential vs scavenge air temperature trend

trace.situation: A tube or end-plate leak develops in the scavenge air cooler, allowing cooling water to enter the scavenge air space. This can cause water ingestion into the cylinders, risking water hammer, liner scuffing, or severe corrosion if not promptly detected.
trace.trigger: Unusually high water level alarm from the drain box level switch or visible excess water in the water mist catcher drain

procedures.action: Confirm the drain box high level alarm and check the volume and rate of water collected over a short period.
procedures.why: Distinguishes a developing tube leak from normal condensate carryover during humid conditions.

procedures.action: Reduce load and prepare to stop the engine if water ingress is confirmed to be from the cooler rather than condensation.
procedures.why: Running with cooling water entering the scavenge air space risks hydraulic lock in a cylinder and severe mechanical damage.

procedures.action: At standstill, pressure test the scavenge air cooler water side to locate the leaking tube or gasket and isolate or plug as required before repair.
procedures.why: Identifies and isolates the specific leak path to allow safe repair or temporary tube plugging.

constraints: Drain box level switch must be operational to detect excessive water accumulation
Engine must not continue running with confirmed water ingress into the scavenge air space
regulations: Manufacturer safety requirement to stop engine on confirmed water ingress into scavenge air space
warnings: Water entering a cylinder through the scavenge ports can cause hydraulic lock, bent connecting rod, or cracked piston crown if the engine continues running
outcomes: Ignoring the leak risks catastrophic mechanical damage to the affected cylinder unit
Early detection and cooler repair avoids major damage and limits downtime to cooler element repair
key_facts: The drain box is equipped with a level switch to indicate excessive water level
Normal operation drain via 'AL' is routed through an orifice to limit scavenge air loss, not for emergency volumes

question_seeds.text: What is the correct response if the drain box level switch indicates abnormally high water accumulation?
Why is a scavenge air cooler tube leak considered an emergency stop condition?

known_issue.failure_mode: scavenge air cooler tube/gasket leak (water ingress)
known_issue.detection_method: drain box high level switch alarm

trace.situation: Sludge and oil residue accumulate in the scavenge air box continuous drain line, partially blocking flow to the pressurised drain tank. This causes a backup of sludge in the scavenge air box area and increases fire risk from accumulated combustible deposits.
trace.trigger: Reduced or stopped flow observed from the scavenge air box drain sight glass or increasing sludge buildup noted during routine inspection

procedures.action: Apply steam to the drain line via the 'BV' connection to help clear the blockage while the engine is running.
procedures.why: Steam assistance is the designed method to facilitate draining when sludge viscosity or buildup restricts flow.

procedures.action: If steam does not clear the blockage, schedule a manual clean of the drain line and drain tank at the next opportunity.
procedures.why: Mechanical blockages such as solidified sludge may require physical removal that steam alone cannot clear.

procedures.action: Verify the drain tank is sized appropriately and piping run is as short as practical per the installation to minimize recurrence.
procedures.why: Long piping runs between engine and drain tank increase blockage risk per manufacturer guidance.

constraints: Scavenge air box continuous drain must not be directly connected to the sludge tank due to pressure differences
Drain tank must be rated for the steam or compressed air working pressure applied via the BV connection
regulations: Manufacturer piping design requirement for pressurised drain tank between scavenge air box and sludge tank
warnings: Accumulated combustible sludge deposits in the scavenge air box increase the risk and severity of a scavenge space fire if ignition occurs
outcomes: Continued blockage increases fire risk and can lead to overflow of sludge into the scavenge air space
Clearing the drain restores safe sludge removal and reduces fire hazard
key_facts: The scavenge air box is continuously drained to a pressurised drain tank sized according to cylinder count
Steam can be applied through the BV connection to facilitate draining

question_seeds.text: How do I clear a blocked scavenge air box drain line using the steam assist connection?

known_issue.failure_mode: scavenge air box drain line blockage
known_issue.detection_method: visual inspection of drain sight glass / sludge buildup observation

trace.situation: The water mist catcher in the scavenge air cooler air chamber becomes saturated or its drain orifice partially blocks, allowing excessive moisture carryover into the scavenge air receiver and subsequently into the cylinders. This increases the risk of combustion instability and corrosive wear.
trace.trigger: Increasing drain box water level trend combined with intermittent misfiring or erratic scavenge air pressure readings

procedures.action: Inspect the water mist catcher drain orifice ('AL' line) for partial blockage by sludge or scale.
procedures.why: A restricted orifice prevents proper continuous drainage, allowing moisture to build up and carry over into the receiver.

procedures.action: Clear or replace the orifice and confirm free continuous drainage is re-established.
procedures.why: Restores the designed small continuous bleed that prevents excessive scavenge air loss while still draining moisture.

procedures.action: Monitor cylinder exhaust temperature spread and lubricating oil condition for signs of water contamination following the fix.
procedures.why: Confirms moisture carryover has stopped and no residual water has affected cylinder lubrication or combustion.

constraints: The AL drain orifice must remain sized to minimize major losses of scavenge air while still allowing continuous drainage
regulations: Manufacturer design requirement for continuous water mist catcher drainage via orifice
warnings: Persistent moisture carryover can cause localized corrosion of cylinder liners and erratic combustion across units
outcomes: Unresolved moisture carryover accelerates liner wear and can cause cylinder-to-cylinder load imbalance
Clearing the orifice restores normal moisture separation and stable combustion
key_facts: The water mist catcher separates moisture from scavenge air before the receiver
The AL line is used continuously during running as the normal water mist catcher drain, separate from the chemical cleaning drain function

question_seeds.text: Which drain line component should be checked if water mist catcher drainage appears reduced?

known_issue.failure_mode: water mist catcher drain orifice blockage
known_issue.detection_method: drain box water level trend / combustion irregularity

trace.situation: The level switch on the scavenge air cooler drain box fails in a way that it does not trigger a high-level alarm despite accumulating water, delaying detection of either normal drain blockage or a developing cooler leak.
trace.trigger: No alarm received despite operator finding unusually high water level in drain box during routine rounds

procedures.action: Manually verify actual water level in the drain box against the alarm setpoint during rounds.
procedures.why: Confirms whether the alarm failed to activate or whether the level genuinely has not reached the setpoint.

procedures.action: Test the level switch electrically and mechanically, checking wiring continuity and float movement.
procedures.why: Determines whether the fault is a wiring/electronic failure or a mechanically stuck float.

procedures.action: Replace or recalibrate the level switch and increase manual drain box checks until the alarm is confirmed functional.
procedures.why: Restores automatic detection capability and bridges the gap with manual monitoring until repair is verified.

constraints: Drain box level switch must be functional to provide early warning of excessive water accumulation per design intent
regulations: Manufacturer requirement for functioning level monitoring instrumentation on scavenge air drain systems
warnings: A failed level alarm can mask an underlying cooler tube leak until water ingress becomes severe enough to affect cylinder operation
outcomes: Undetected high level can progress to water carryover into cylinders before being noticed
Repairing the switch restores early warning capability for both blockage and leak conditions
key_facts: The drain box is equipped with a level switch specifically to indicate excessive water level
Manual rounds should include visual verification of drain box level as a backup to automatic alarm

question_seeds.text: How should I verify the drain box level switch is functioning correctly during rounds?

known_issue.failure_mode: drain box level switch malfunction
known_issue.detection_method: manual visual inspection discrepancy with alarm system

trace.situation: A low-order scavenge air space fire occurs due to ignition of oil and carbon deposits on the scavenge air box walls, typically from a leaking piston ring or excessive cylinder lubrication. The fire is detected early before reaching a severe stage but requires immediate corrective action to prevent escalation.
trace.trigger: Scavenge air space high temperature alarm or smoke/odor detected from scavenge drain area with no corresponding change in ambient conditions

procedures.action: Reduce engine load immediately and increase cylinder lubrication temporarily per approved procedure while monitoring the affected area temperature.
procedures.why: Reducing load lowers heat generation and additional lubrication can help suppress smoldering deposits while diagnosing the source.

procedures.action: If temperature continues to rise, stop the engine and prepare the fixed fire extinguishing system (steam, water mist, or CO2) for the scavenge air space per the installed system.
procedures.why: Manual intervention is insufficient if the fire is sustaining itself; the fixed system is designed specifically for this space and situation.

procedures.action: After extinguishing, open and inspect the scavenge air space and ports for the affected unit(s) to identify and correct the root cause, such as a damaged piston ring or scraper ring before restart.
procedures.why: Addresses the underlying mechanical cause of excess oil/deposit buildup to prevent recurrence.

constraints: Steam fire extinguishing system requires 3-10 bar supply pressure and approximately 2.2 kg per cylinder
Engine must be stopped before activating the scavenge air space fire extinguishing system
regulations: SOLAS Chapter II-2 requirement for fixed fire extinguishing arrangements in scavenge air spaces of two-stroke engines
warnings: Opening the scavenge air space covers while a fire is active can introduce oxygen and intensify the fire; engine must be stopped and extinguishing system discharged first
outcomes: Unchecked scavenge fire can escalate to multiple-cylinder damage, warped scavenge box covers, or hull plating heat damage
Early detection and controlled extinguishing limits damage to a single affected unit
key_facts: Scavenge air space fires are typically caused by ignition of accumulated oil deposits from ring blow-by or over-lubrication
The fixed extinguishing system options are steam, water mist, or CO2, each sized per cylinder

question_seeds.text: What is the immediate action if a scavenge air space temperature alarm indicates a possible fire?
Why must the engine be stopped before discharging the scavenge air space fire extinguishing system?

known_issue.failure_mode: scavenge air space fire (low order)
known_issue.detection_method: scavenge space temperature alarm / smoke detection

trace.situation: A severe scavenge air space fire develops rapidly, likely from a ruptured piston ring or sustained oil leak, causing a pressure spike that lifts the scavenge air space explosion relief/door. This represents a serious casualty risk with potential for structural damage and crew injury if personnel are nearby.
trace.trigger: Explosion relief valve/door lift alarm or audible bang from the scavenge air space combined with a sharp scavenge air pressure spike

procedures.action: Immediately stop the engine and ensure all personnel are clear of the scavenge air space area and relief door locations.
procedures.why: A lifted relief device indicates a significant pressure event that may repeat; personnel safety takes priority over continued operation.

procedures.action: Activate the fixed scavenge air space fire extinguishing system (steam, water mist, or CO2) per the installed configuration.
procedures.why: A relief door lift strongly indicates an active fire or explosion event inside the scavenge space requiring full suppression.

procedures.action: After the space has cooled and been confirmed fire-free, conduct a full internal inspection of all scavenge ports, cooler, and affected unit components before any restart is considered.
procedures.why: A pressure event of this severity likely caused mechanical damage requiring repair verification prior to returning to service.

constraints: Explosion relief doors are designed to lift at a specific overpressure threshold and must be reset/inspected before restart
Engine must remain stopped until the space is confirmed safe for entry and inspection
regulations: SOLAS Chapter II-2 requirement for explosion relief valves on crankcase/scavenge spaces of large engines
Classification society survey requirement for inspection after a scavenge space explosion event
warnings: Never attempt to restart the engine or open covers without confirming the fire is fully extinguished and the space has cooled, as reignition or secondary explosion risk is high
outcomes: Failure to fully investigate and repair before restart risks repeat failure and potential total loss of the affected cylinder unit
Thorough inspection and repair following a controlled response allows safe return to service
key_facts: CO2 fire extinguishing requires approximately 4.3 kg per cylinder at a 150 bar test pressure for the system
A relief door lift is a strong indicator of a significant internal pressure event requiring full investigation

question_seeds.text: When is it safe to restart the engine after a scavenge air space explosion relief door has lifted?
